_comment: Maintenance Plan generator. Authored at the Phase 2 assessability floor; pairs with PE (MA-5 maintenance personnel use the PE-3 escort policy), PS (MA-5 maintenance personnel are subject to PS-3 / PS-7 screening), MP (MA-3(2) media inspection echoes MP-5 transport handling; MA-2 sanitization before maintenance overlaps MP-6), and CM (MA-2 maintenance records feed CM-3 change control). Compact family — 6 base controls at moderate; the rigor is in vendor escort + remote-maintenance protections.
title: Maintenance Plan
description: Documents how the system's maintenance activities are governed across scheduling, tool control, nonlocal (remote) maintenance, maintenance personnel, and timely component replacement. Covers the controls of the MA family in NIST SP 800-53 r5 and aligns with NIST SP 800-88 r1 (Sanitization), NIST SP 800-46 r2 (Remote Access), CNSSP-300 (Hardware Maintenance for National Security Systems), and FAR / DFARS clauses governing vendor maintenance personnel.
intro_template:
This Maintenance Plan documents the maintenance approach for {system_name}. It establishes the practices, tooling, cadences, and roles used to schedule and record maintenance, control maintenance tools and the media they introduce or remove, secure nonlocal (remote) maintenance sessions, manage maintenance personnel including vendor staff, and ensure timely replacement of system components requiring maintenance.

The scope covers controlled maintenance per MA-2, maintenance tools per MA-3, nonlocal maintenance per MA-4, maintenance personnel per MA-5, and timely maintenance per MA-6 within the {system_name} authorization boundary. The plan is consistent with NIST SP 800-53 r5 (Maintenance family), NIST SP 800-88 r1 (Sanitization Guidelines for sanitization before vendor maintenance), and CNSSP-300 (Hardware Maintenance) for classified systems where applicable.
approach_template:
{system_name} schedules and records maintenance through {maintenance_scheduling_system}. Maintenance vendors are managed via {vendor_management_role} with escort policy coordinated with §4 of the PE plan. Nonlocal (remote) maintenance is performed over {nonlocal_channel} with the safeguards in §4.4. Spare-parts inventory for timely maintenance is maintained at {spares_inventory_location} with the SLAs in §4.6.

Additional details on controlled maintenance, maintenance tools, nonlocal maintenance, maintenance personnel, and timely maintenance are captured in the sub-sections below.
continuous_monitoring_template: Maintenance performance for {system_name} is tracked through the metrics in §6.1 (maintenance-window adherence rate, mean time between failures, mean time to repair, vendor-escort completion rate, sanitization-before-vendor-maintenance compliance, nonlocal-maintenance session anomalies). Maintenance records are reviewed on the cadence in §6.2; vendor-personnel rosters are reconciled with the PS-7 external-personnel register and with the PE-2 access list to surface drift.
integration_template: This Maintenance Plan does not stand alone. The PE family supplies the PE-3 escort policy and PE-2 access authorization for maintenance personnel; the PS family supplies the PS-3 / PS-7 screening that underwrites maintenance-personnel access; the MP family handles the media that MA-3(2) inspects and MA-2 sanitization-before-maintenance protects; the CM family receives MA-2 maintenance records as inputs to CM-3 change-control where maintenance produces configuration changes; the IR family escalates anomalies detected during maintenance (tampered tools, unauthorized media, suspicious nonlocal sessions). The following cross-references identify the specific artifacts and locations where MA-related content is exchanged with other RMF deliverables.

commonly_inheritable_controls.from: Hosting provider (when system runs on cloud / colocation — provider performs hardware maintenance)
Hosting provider (cloud / colo — provider tools, not system-managed)

family_questions.label: Approach basics
family_questions.description: Tooling and roles that anchor the rest of the plan.

questions.label: Maintenance scheduling system (one-liner)
questions.help: Where maintenance is scheduled and recorded (e.g., 'ServiceNow CMDB + Change module', 'Maximo CMMS', 'Inherited from cloud provider — no system-managed hardware').

questions.label: Maintenance-vendor management role
questions.help: Role accountable for vendor maintenance personnel (e.g., 'Facilities Operations Manager + Contracting Officer', 'ISSO with PSO support').

questions.label: Nonlocal-maintenance channel
questions.help: How remote maintenance reaches system components (e.g., 'GFE-laptop + agency VPN with MFA + session recording', 'Vendor-side privileged-access workstation through bastion'). Reference the SC plan for transmission protections.

questions.label: Spare-parts inventory location
questions.help: Where spare components are inventoried (e.g., 'Onsite cage + cloud-provider auto-replacement; CMDB tracks individual spares by serial').

questions.label: Hosting-inheritance summary
questions.help: One-line summary of which MA controls are inherited from the hosting provider (e.g., 'MA-2 / MA-3 inherited from AWS; system-managed for endpoint workstations only').

family_questions.label: Controlled Maintenance (MA-2)
family_questions.description: Scheduling, approval, recording, and post-maintenance security.

questions.label: Maintenance approval workflow
questions.help: How maintenance is approved before execution (e.g., 'CCB approves planned maintenance windows; emergency maintenance requires retroactive approval within 24h'). Reference CM-3 for change-control overlap.

questions.label: Pre-vendor-maintenance sanitization
questions.help: How information is sanitized from a component before vendor maintenance (especially when component leaves the facility). Reference NIST SP 800-88 r1 categories (Clear / Purge / Destroy).

questions.label: Post-maintenance security check
questions.help: Verification that security controls remain intact after maintenance (FIM check, configuration-baseline verification, integrity scan). Reference SI-7 for integrity verification.

questions.label: Maintenance-record retention
questions.help: How long maintenance records are retained. Reference NARA records-retention schedule.

family_questions.label: Maintenance Tools (MA-3)
family_questions.description: Tool inventory, inspection, and media handling.

questions.label: Tool-modification inspection (MA-3(1))
questions.help: How maintenance tools are inspected for improper modifications before use. Tamper-evident packaging, vendor-supplied integrity hashes.

questions.label: Media-inspection for malicious code (MA-3(2))
questions.help: How media brought in for diagnostics (USB, CDs, etc.) is scanned for malware before use. Dedicated scan-station, write-blocked-read.

questions.label: Unauthorized-removal prevention (MA-3(3))
questions.help: How equipment is checked at removal (per MA-3(3)) — verify the component or media is sanitized or authorized for removal. Coordinated with PE-16.

questions.label: Tool storage location
questions.help: Where maintenance tools are stored when not in use (locked cabinet, controlled checkout system).

family_questions.label: Nonlocal Maintenance (MA-4)
family_questions.description: Remote / vendor maintenance over network channels.

questions.label: Session-initiation workflow
questions.help: How a nonlocal maintenance session is initiated (e.g., 'Vendor requests via Service Now → ISSO approval → just-in-time bastion access opened for the window → revoked at session end').

questions.label: Session protections in place
options: Bastion / jump-server enforced (no direct vendor → host)
Endpoint posture check on vendor device

questions.label: Session-disconnect verification
questions.help: How session termination is verified (no lingering processes, no re-auth credentials cached).

questions.label: Session-recording retention
questions.help: How long nonlocal-maintenance session recordings are retained. Useful for after-action review when anomalies are reported. Reference AU plan.

questions.label: Classified-system nonlocal-maintenance handling
questions.help: If applicable: special handling per CNSSP-300. Often non-local maintenance is prohibited on classified systems.

family_questions.label: Maintenance Personnel (MA-5)
family_questions.description: Vendor staff governance, escort, and access.

questions.label: Personnel screening requirement
questions.help: Required background-investigation level for maintenance personnel. Reference PS-3 / PS-7 standards. Cleared vs uncleared personnel handling.

questions.label: Escort policy
options: All vendor staff escorted at all times (default)
Cleared vendor staff unescorted in approved areas; uncleared escorted
Escort required only in sensitive zones; perimeter areas free
No escort required (vendor fully cleared + indoctrinated)

questions.label: Vendor-authorization process
questions.help: How specific vendor employees are authorized for access (vendor-supplied roster, PIV-I cards, agency-issued temporary badges). Reference PS-7.

questions.label: Temporary-access provisioning SLA
questions.help: Time from vendor-personnel-change notification to access record updated. Common: 'Within 1 business day'.

questions.label: Post-visit review
questions.help: How vendor visits are reviewed after the fact (escort log review, surveillance review for anomalies, badge-event reconciliation).

questions.label: Critical-component register (MA-6 ODV)
questions.help: Components for which timely-maintenance SLAs apply. MA-6 ODV — system components requiring obtainable spare parts within an organization-defined time period.

questions.label: Replacement SLA by component class
questions.help: Time within which each component class must be replaceable. Example: 'HSM: 24h; production database server: 4h via cloud-provider auto-replacement; network appliance: 72h with vendor next-business-day support contract'.

questions.label: Spare-inventory strategy
options: Onsite cold spares for critical components
Vendor-managed inventory with N4H delivery contract
Mixed (onsite for critical; vendor-managed for non-critical)

questions.label: Spare-test cadence
questions.help: How often spares are tested to ensure they are functional when needed (rotation schedule, periodic boot test).

family_questions.label: Maintenance Scope and Coverage
family_questions.description: Quantitative scope numbers that anchor metrics later in the plan.

questions.label: System components requiring maintenance
questions.help: Approximate count of components that need MA-2 controlled-maintenance handling.

questions.label: Maintenance vendors / personnel count
questions.help: Approximate count of vendor maintenance personnel with system access (PS-7).

questions.label: Nonlocal-maintenance session volume
questions.help: Approximate sessions per quarter (anchors session-recording storage planning).

questions.label: Critical components with spares
questions.help: Count of components covered by spare-parts inventory (MA-6).

family_questions.label: Maintenance Metrics & KPIs
family_questions.description: Metrics tracked to demonstrate MA control effectiveness.

questions.label: Tracked metrics
suggestions: Maintenance-window adherence rate (% scheduled vs ad-hoc)
Vendor-escort completion rate (% sessions with escort logged)
Open POA&M items linked to MA controls

family_questions.label: Maintenance Anomaly Detection
family_questions.description: How anomalies in maintenance activity are detected and escalated.

questions.label: Escalation path
questions.help: How detected anomalies escalate (typically to the IR plan workflow). Severity classification.

family_questions.label: Cross-references to other RMF artifacts
family_questions.description: Where this plan plugs into the broader RMF package.

questions.label: SSP section reference
questions.help: Where in the SSP the MA control implementations are summarized (e.g., 'SSP §13.7').

questions.label: POA&M ID prefix for MA findings
questions.help: Convention for MA-related POA&M items (e.g., 'POAM-MA-' for general).

questions.label: PE handoff
questions.help: How MA-5 maintenance personnel use the PE-3 escort policy and PE-2 access list. Vendor-visit coordination.

questions.label: PS handoff
questions.help: How MA-5 maintenance personnel are screened per PS-3 / PS-7. Trigger when vendor personnel change.

questions.label: MP handoff
questions.help: How MA-3(2) media inspection coordinates with MP-5 transport handling and MA-2 pre-maintenance sanitization with MP-6 sanitization.

questions.label: CM handoff
questions.help: How MA-2 maintenance records feed CM-3 change control where maintenance produces configuration changes.

questions.label: IR handoff
questions.help: How maintenance anomalies (tampered tools, unauthorized media, anomalous nonlocal sessions) escalate into the IR plan.

questions.label: CA-7 continuous-monitoring strategy reference
questions.help: Pointer to the CA-7 monitoring strategy document tying MA continuous-monitoring metrics to the broader ConMon plan.

glossary.definition: An intermediate access-controlled host through which maintenance sessions to internal components are routed. Common MA-4 protection.
Documented sequence of transfers of an asset from one custodian to another. Critical when components leave the facility for maintenance.
Configuration Management Database / Computerized Maintenance Management System — systems tracking components, their state, and maintenance history.
Committee on National Security Systems Policy 300 — Hardware Maintenance for National Security Systems. Applies special handling for classified systems.
A replacement component kept in storage, ready for installation when the primary fails. Contrast with hot spare (already powered and standby) and warm spare (powered but not active).
Access credentials provisioned only for the duration of a maintenance window, automatically revoked at session end. Common MA-4 protection.
Mean Time Between Failures — average time between failures of a component or system. Drives MA-6 spare-inventory planning.
Mean Time to Repair — average time required to restore a component to operation after a failure. Tracked as an MA-6 metric.
Per MA-4, maintenance performed over a network connection from a location not within the system's physical boundary. Subject to specific protections including session recording and JIT access.

Personal Identity Verification - Interoperable — credential standard allowing non-federal organizations to issue PIV-equivalent credentials trusted by federal systems. Common for vendor staff requiring repeat access.
Per MA-6(1), scheduled maintenance performed to prevent failures (firmware updates, fan replacement, battery replacement) rather than to fix existing problems.
Per MA-6(2), maintenance triggered by analytics predicting an impending failure (SMART drive analytics, thermal trends, vendor-supplied predictive models).

Process of removing data from media to prevent recovery. Per NIST SP 800-88 r1: Clear (logical), Purge (cryptographic erase / degauss), Destroy (physical destruction). Required by MA-2 before vendor-maintained components leave the facility.
Capture of activity (keyboard, screen, network traffic) during a maintenance session, enabling after-action review. Common MA-4 protection.
Per MA-6, the time within which a replacement component must be obtainable for a given system component class. Tied to organizational MTTR objectives.
Packaging that displays visible evidence if opened. Common method for verifying maintenance-tool integrity per MA-3(1).
Scheduled maintenance window during which the system remains in production but at reduced capacity. Distinct from cold (powered down) and hot (no impact) windows.
